Apis mellifera.primary_hazard: Venomous sting causing localized pain, swelling, and potential systemic anaphylaxis in allergic individuals.
Apis mellifera.disclaimer: This first-aid guide is for informational purposes only and does not replace professional medical advice.
immediate_steps: CALL EMERGENCY SERVICES (e.g., 911/112) IMMEDIATELY if the victim shows signs of anaphylaxis (difficulty breathing, swelling of throat/face, hives, dizziness).
Remove the stinger immediately. Scraping it off flatly with a fingernail, credit card, or blunt knife is preferred.
Wash the sting area thoroughly with clean water and mild soap to prevent infection.
Apply a cold pack or ice wrapped in a thin cloth to the area for 10-15 minutes to reduce localized swelling and numb pain.
critical_warnings: DO NOT use tweezers or your fingers to pinch and squeeze the stinger, as this may inject more venom from the venom sac.
DO NOT scratch the sting site, as this will worsen localized irritation and may introduce bacterial infections.
paramedic_checklist: Note the exact time of the sting.
Monitor for progressive allergic reactions, airway constriction, or hives.
Confirm if the patient has a known bee allergy or carries an Epinephrine Auto-Injector (EpiPen).

Crotalus oreganus.primary_hazard: Venomous hemotoxic and tissue-destroying bite. Left untreated, it can be lethal or lead to limb loss.
Crotalus oreganus.disclaimer: All snakebites must be treated as medical emergencies. Seek professional hospital care immediately.
immediate_steps: CALL EMERGENCY SERVICES (e.g., 911/112) IMMEDIATELY.
Keep the victim calm, warm, and as still as possible. Movement speeds up the circulation of venom.
Keep the bitten limb positioned at or slightly below heart level to slow venom progression.
Remove all rings, watches, bracelets, or tight clothing from the bitten limb immediately before swelling begins.
Wash the bite site gently with soap and water if available, and cover it with a loose, clean, dry bandage.
critical_warnings: DO NOT use a tourniquet or tie any restrictive bands, as trapping the venom in a small area increases severe tissue damage.
DO NOT cut the wound or attempt to suck out the venom by mouth or mechanical suction devices.
DO NOT apply ice or submerge the wound in water.
DO NOT give the victim pain medication, stimulants, alcohol, or caffeine, which can elevate heart rate.
paramedic_checklist: Note the exact time of the bite.
Track and mark the borders of swelling and discoloration with a pen every 15 minutes to monitor venom activity.
Do not try to capture or kill the snake. If safe, a quick photo can help the medical team identify the species.

Trimeresurus sabahi fucatus.primary_hazard: Venomous hematoxic bite causing severe swelling, pain, internal bleeding, and tissue necrosis.
Trimeresurus sabahi fucatus.disclaimer: All pit viper bites are severe medical emergencies. Immediate antivenom administration is required.
immediate_steps: CALL EMERGENCY SERVICES (e.g., 911/112) IMMEDIATELY.
Keep the bitten limb completely immobilized and positioned below heart level to slow venom circulation.
Do NOT move the patient unless absolutely necessary. Keep them resting quietly.
Remove tight bands, rings, and clothing immediately as rapid swelling is expected.
Gently clean the bite area and apply a clean, dry dressing.
critical_warnings: DO NOT cut the bite site or attempt to suck the venom out by mouth.
DO NOT apply ice, electricity, or tourniquets, which can cause severe localized tissue necrosis.
DO NOT administer aspirin or other blood-thinning painkillers.
paramedic_checklist: Note the exact time of the bite and onset of systemic bleeding signs.
Prepare for rapid IV fluid access and monitor coagulation profiles.
Assess and document progressive swelling borders every 15 minutes.

Latrodectus mactans.primary_hazard: Neurotoxic venomous bite causing severe localized pain, muscle cramping, abdominal rigidity, and hypertension.
Latrodectus mactans.disclaimer: Bites from black widows are medical emergencies requiring close observation and potential antivenom therapy.
immediate_steps: CALL EMERGENCY SERVICES (e.g., 911/112) IMMEDIATELY.
Wash the spider bite area thoroughly with soap and water.
Apply a cold damp cloth or ice pack wrapped in a washcloth to the bite site to relieve swelling and throbbing.
Keep the bitten limb elevated to reduce localized pressure.
Observe the patient closely for spreading pain, chest/abdominal tightness, or muscle spasms.
critical_warnings: DO NOT use a tourniquet or squeeze/cut the bite area.
DO NOT apply heat packs, which can accelerate the spread of neurotoxins in the bloodstream.
paramedic_checklist: Note the time of the bite and onset of systemic symptoms.
Monitor blood pressure closely, as black widow venom can cause significant hypertensive episodes.
Assess for muscle rigidity, particularly in the abdomen, which can mimic appendicitis.

Ursus arctos horribilis.primary_hazard: Physical trauma, severe lacerations, puncture wounds, crushing force, and heavy bleeding.
Ursus arctos horribilis.disclaimer: Bear maulings cause severe multi-system trauma. Immediate surgical intervention is critical.
immediate_steps: CALL EMERGENCY SERVICES (e.g., 911/112) IMMEDIATELY.
Ensure the scene is safe. Do not approach the victim if the bear is still active or visible.
Apply firm, direct pressure to any actively bleeding wounds using clean cloth, sterile dressings, or hands.
Elevate bleeding extremities above heart level if no fractures are suspected.
Keep the victim lying down, warm (cover with blankets/jackets), and still to prevent shock.
critical_warnings: DO NOT wash out deep puncture wounds or internal tissues in the field, as this can introduce deep-seated pathogens.
DO NOT move the victim if spinal, neck, or head injuries are suspected, unless they are in immediate danger of another attack.
paramedic_checklist: Estimate total blood loss and note locations of deep puncture wounds or crushing fractures.
Immobilize the cervical spine if structural impact is suspected.
